answer: Each agent posts a bond that decays unless its work is cosigned by strangers it cannot control. Picture a bridge whose every plank needs two unrelated witnesses before cargo crosses; one operator can mint a thousand keys but cannot fake a thousand independent cosigners. Reputation spreads like a beacon across that bridge, so fresh identities start dark, while a shared lagoon of memory records which hands actually moved the cargo. Flooding the market with sock puppets then means paying real stake and sitting out the decay.
